note: Language Hierarchy configures parent/child fallback between languages. A language's parent is stored as a third-party setting on its configurable_language config entity: third_party_settings.language_hierarchy.fallback_langcode. hook_language_fallback_candidates_alter walks that chain to build fallback candidates (check via \Drupal::languageManager()->getFallbackCandidates(['langcode'=>...])); the module also maintains a language_hierarchy_priority DB table rebuilt on any language insert/update/delete and config import, and applies fallback to config translation (config factory override), interface strings (locale.storage decorator), and path aliases. No settings form, no permission of its own; configured through the core language forms. Provides a Views sort (language_hierarchy_sort) and filter (language_hierarchy_content_language_fallback_limited). Eval cases use custom langcodes lhp/lhm/lhc (namespaced with 'lh') created and deleted by the scripts; medium reads a real configured fallback back, hard sets a fallback and builds a multi-level chain verified through the live language manager.

evals.prompt: Using the language_hierarchy module, how do I make one language fall back to another (its parent), and where is that relationship stored?
evals.expected_output: Set the child language's parent via the 'Translation fallback language' select on the language edit form (or the parent/child tree on the languages overview). It is stored as a third-party setting on the configurable_language entity: third_party_settings.language_hierarchy.fallback_langcode.

evals.prompt: With language_hierarchy configured, how does Drupal decide the fallback order for a language, and how can I inspect the resolved fallback chain for a given langcode?
evals.expected_output: The module implements hook_language_fallback_candidates_alter() to walk the fallback_langcode chain; you can inspect the result with \Drupal::languageManager()->getFallbackCandidates(['langcode' => '<lc>']), which returns the ordered candidate list (e.g. de-at, de, en, und).

evals.prompt: Besides content translation, what else does the language_hierarchy fallback apply to, and what internal table does it maintain to order fallbacks?
evals.expected_output: Fallback applies to configuration translation (config factory override), interface/locale string translation (locale.storage decorator, when locale is on) and path aliases. It maintains the language_hierarchy_priority table (langcode -> priority), rebuilt on any language change or config import.

evals.prompt: This site has a language with langcode 'lhc' whose fallback is configured via language_hierarchy. Inspect the live configuration and state which language 'lhc' falls back to.
evals.expected_output: lhc falls back to lhp: configurable_language.lhc has third_party_settings.language_hierarchy.fallback_langcode = 'lhp'.

evals.prompt: On this site a multi-level language fallback chain is configured with language_hierarchy starting from langcode 'lhc'. Inspect the running site and list the languages 'lhc' will fall back through, in order.
evals.expected_output: lhc falls back through lhm then lhp: the resolved fallback candidates for lhc are lhc, lhm, lhp (then und). Discoverable via \Drupal::languageManager()->getFallbackCandidates(['langcode' => 'lhc']).

evals.prompt: This site has two languages, langcodes 'lhp' and 'lhc'. Using the language_hierarchy module, configure 'lhc' so that it falls back to 'lhp' when a translation is missing. Apply the change to the live site.
My site has three languages with codes lhp, lhm and lhc. I want it so that if something isn't translated into lhc it tries lhm next, and if lhm doesn't have it either it uses lhp. Set that up.
evals.expected_output: lhc's fallback is lhm and lhm's fallback is lhp, so \Drupal::languageManager()->getFallbackCandidates(['langcode' => 'lhc']) yields lhc, lhm, lhp (then und).
